operations.name: Suggest options from a website
operations.agentTask: Read the website in `sourceUrl` and write three different ways to fill the ad "Binary-choice participation card". Objective: Invite a clear A/B response without pretending an MP4 is interactive. Visual rule: The two choices have equal visual weight and remain visible long enough to answer. Beats, in order: - 0–2 s: Context image and one short question. Shows Brand color, Context image, Question. - 2–4 s: Left/top card appears with a simple visual. Shows Brand color, Choice A, Choice A text. - 4–6 s: Right/bottom card appears in the matching treatment. Shows Brand color, Choice B, Choice B text. - 6–8 s: Both choices are shown together. Shows Brand color, Choice A, Choice B, Compare prompt. - 8–10 s: Explicit instruction: comment A/B, or use a configured native poll. Shows Brand color, Choice A, Choice B, Logo, Participation call to action. Use only facts the website or pages you read state. Never invent prices, discounts, dates, guarantees or claims. When a fact a field needs is missing, write a short placeholder in square brackets, such as [offer end date]. Make the three options clearly different in angle, wording and image choice. For images, choose real, large images of this brand and product: first from the page's own images (header logo, large files, feature-page screenshots), then with an image search. A social preview card (og:image, a title on a gradient) is a last resort. Give the direct URL of the image file, never a page URL, and never an image of another brand. Use an empty string when no image fits. If image search throws because no search backend is configured, tell the user in one sentence that a SerpAPI, DataForSEO or Brave key in Settings finds better images. Then take nodetool.web.screenshot of the product's feature pages instead. Save each image you consider as an asset and look at it with view_image before you offer it. Name in the option's description any image that is only a social preview card. Write `fillOptions` as a list of three objects, `fillChoice` as "" and `fillReport` as "". Each option: - value: "1", "2" or "3" - title: a name for the direction in 2 to 4 words - description: one sentence on what it emphasizes, then the first two copy lines in quotes - image: the URL of its first image, for the option card - brandColor: the brand's accent color as #RRGGBB (buttons, links, highlights), not the page background or a theme-color that is near black or white - fields: question (Question: question, at most 7 words); choiceA (Choice A text: choice a, at most 7 words); choiceB (Choice B text: choice b, at most 7 words); comparePrompt (Compare prompt: compare, at most 7 words); participationCta (Participation call to action: cta, at most 8 words) - images: contextImage (Context image: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Context image and one short question.); choiceAImage (Choice A: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Left/top card appears with a simple visual. | Both choices are shown together. | Explicit instruction: comment A/B, or use a configured native poll.); choiceBImage (Choice B: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Right/bottom card appears in the matching treatment. | Both choices are shown together. | Explicit instruction: comment A/B, or use a configured native poll.); logo (Logo: The brand's own logo file, such as the site header logo or its icon. Shown in: Explicit instruction: comment A/B, or use a configured native poll.) Then show the Start step with `only: ["fillChoice"]` and a one-sentence note, so the user sees just the option cards. Picking one runs `apply`, which saves the images and fills the steps.
